_comment: Artifact types the adapter recognises. The list is ordered: a file takes the first type whose rules match, so specific types come before general ones.
A type matches when any one of its rules matches. A rule matches when every condition it lists holds:
names: the file name matches one of these globs (case-insensitive).
magic: the file starts with one of these byte signatures at the given offset.
hive:  the file is a registry hive whose embedded name or file name matches one of these globs.
sidecars: suffixes that, appended to the file name, name companion files staged together with it.

artifacts.label: Registry transaction log
artifacts.about: Changes Windows wrote to a hive's log before flushing them into the hive. The adapter stages these next to their hive automatically so parsers can replay them.

artifacts.label: Registry: Amcache.hve
artifacts.about: Inventory of programs and executables Windows has seen, with SHA-1 hashes, paths and first-seen times.

artifacts.label: Registry: SYSTEM
artifacts.about: Machine configuration: services, devices, USB history, time zone, network interfaces and the ShimCache (AppCompatCache) execution list.

artifacts.label: Registry: SOFTWARE
artifacts.about: Installed software, OS version, autostart locations and network profiles. Also used to resolve application names in SRUM.

artifacts.label: Registry: SAM
artifacts.about: Local user accounts, group membership, last logon times and logon counts.

artifacts.label: Registry: SECURITY
artifacts.about: Local security policy, audit policy and cached domain logon data.

artifacts.label: Registry: NTUSER.DAT
artifacts.about: One user's settings and activity: recent documents, typed paths, UserAssist run counts, mounted devices and more.

artifacts.label: Registry: UsrClass.dat
artifacts.about: One user's class registrations. Holds the ShellBags that record which folders the user opened, including on removed drives.

artifacts.label: Registry: other hive
artifacts.about: Any other registry hive, such as DEFAULT, BCD, COMPONENTS or settings.dat.

artifacts.label: NTFS $MFT
artifacts.about: The NTFS Master File Table: one record per file and folder on the volume, with names, sizes and timestamps, including many deleted entries.

artifacts.label: NTFS $J (USN journal)
artifacts.about: The NTFS change journal: a log of file creations, renames, writes and deletions. A $MFT from the same volume resolves the parent folder paths.

artifacts.label: NTFS $Boot
artifacts.about: The NTFS boot sector: volume serial number, cluster size and the location of the $MFT.

artifacts.label: NTFS $SDS
artifacts.about: The NTFS security descriptor stream: owners and access control lists referenced by $MFT records.

artifacts.label: NTFS $I30 index
artifacts.about: A directory index. Its slack space can still list files that were deleted from the folder.

artifacts.label: Prefetch
artifacts.about: Written when a program starts. Records the run count, up to eight last run times and the files the program loaded.

artifacts.label: Shortcut (LNK)
artifacts.about: Shortcut files, many created automatically when a user opens a document. They keep the target path, its timestamps and the volume it lived on.

artifacts.label: Jump list
artifacts.about: Per-application lists of recently and frequently opened files, shown in the taskbar. Each entry embeds a shortcut with timestamps.

artifacts.label: Windows event log
artifacts.about: Windows event logs: logons, process creation, service installs, PowerShell, RDP and many other system and security events.

artifacts.label: SRUM database
artifacts.about: System Resource Usage Monitor: per-application network traffic, CPU time and energy use, kept for about 30 days. A SOFTWARE hive resolves application and user names.

artifacts.label: User Access Logging
artifacts.about: Windows Server User Access Logging databases: which clients and users connected to server roles, and when.

artifacts.label: Windows Search index
artifacts.about: The Windows Search database. Lists indexed files with metadata, internet history and activity history, even for files that are gone.

artifacts.label: Windows Timeline
artifacts.about: ActivitiesCache.db: the Windows Timeline of applications used and documents opened, with focus durations.

artifacts.label: Recycle Bin record
artifacts.about: Recycle Bin metadata ($I files, or INFO2 on Windows XP): the original path, size and deletion time of each deleted file.

artifacts.label: RecentFileCache.bcf
artifacts.about: Windows 7 list of recently executed programs, the predecessor of Amcache.

artifacts.label: SQLite database
artifacts.about: SQLite databases, such as browser history, cookies, downloads and many application stores.

artifacts.label: Memory image
artifacts.about: A capture of physical memory: running processes, network connections, command lines and injected code at the time of capture.

artifacts.label: Executable (PE)
artifacts.about: Windows programs and libraries (EXE, DLL, SYS). Triage covers signatures, hashes, compiler and packer, and embedded strings.

artifacts.label: Document
artifacts.about: PDF, Office and RTF documents. Their metadata can name the author, the software used and creation and edit times.

artifacts.label: Image or media
artifacts.about: Photos, audio and video. Their metadata can hold the capture time, camera model and GPS position.
